# EC49FVE — coupled numerator valuations and a four-prime exceptional-width witness

2026-11-21 (Asia/Shanghai). Evidence: **AUTHOR_PROVED / EXACT_FRACTION_FINITE_CROSSCHECK / PARENT_DEPENDENT / NOT_REVIEWED / NOT_ADMITTED**.

## Provenance and model

Independent *portable scientific continuation* of [EC49FVD](https://github.com/awdawmip/enterprise-math/pull/2873), immutable predecessor commit \`21c04a1b119b700b88a8de44ffdf5e0cda184438\`. Scientific input is frozen **BRC16943** at \`fc0f038e7bfd12c886b4d37f900bfb770c0f61ab\`. P000/ACTIVE world assumptions and present control policies are current-read context, not new scientific pins. The object proved below is the *derived Bernoulli hit observer*, not a native six-axis event or physical time. Full composite minimax transfer remains conditional on the unreviewed FUQ/FUR endpoint-reduction results.

Set, exactly,
\[
\beta=\frac3{637},\qquad\gamma=\frac{141024}{1653649},\qquad u=\frac{4822040484}{8132285009},
\]
\[
T_0=(1-x)(1-\beta x),\quad T_E=(1-x)(1+\gamma x),\quad
a=1-T_0=\frac{x(640-3x)}{637},\quad b=1-uT_E,
\]
\[
R=\frac{T_0}{uT_E},\quad S=\frac{bR}{a},\qquad
t(x)=\frac{\log R}{\log S}.
\]
For every reduced rational \(x=m/d\in(0,1)\), frozen strict probability ordering gives \(1<R<S\) and \(0<t(x)<1\). If \(t=h/k\in\mathbb Q\), then \(0<h<k\), and for **every rational prime** \(p\),
\[
k\,v_p(R)=h\,v_p(S). \tag{1}
\]
This is a necessary *simultaneous* valuation condition, not a sufficiency test.

## Theorem 1 — joint 2-adic / 3-adic numerator synchronization

Suppose \(6\mid m\) and \(\gcd(m,d)=1\); hence \(d\) is a 2-/3-unit. Put
\(A=v_2(a)>0\) and \(q=v_3(m)>0\). Then **exactly**
\[
(v_2(R),v_2(S))=(-2,-2-A),\qquad
(v_3(R),v_3(S))=(-6,-6-q). \tag{2}
\]
Consequently
\[
\boxed{q\ne3A\quad\Longrightarrow\quad t(m/d)\notin\mathbb Q.} \tag{3}
\]
When \(q=3A\), (2) alone leaves the question open: it does not construct a rational phase.

**Proof.** Since \(x\) is 2-adically even, \(1-x\), \(1-\beta x\), and \(1+\gamma x\) are 2-units; \(v_2(u)=2\), while \(b=1-uT_E\) is a 2-unit. Thus \(v_2(R)=-2\) and \(v_2(S)=-2-v_2(a)\). For \(3\mid m\), similarly \(1-x,1-\beta x,1+\gamma x\) are 3-units, \(v_3(u)=6\), and \(b\) is a 3-unit. Since \(\beta\) has \(v_3(\beta)=1\), the factor \(1+\beta-\beta x\) is a 3-unit; hence \(v_3(a)=v_3(x)=q\), establishing (2). If (1) holds, the 2-adic equation forces \(h/k=2/(2+A)\), and the 3-adic equation forces \(h/k=6/(6+q)\). Equality yields \(q=3A\). QED.

The 2-adic exponent is explicitly computable from \(j=v_2(m)\ge1\) (because \(d\) is odd):
\[
A=j+v_2(640-3x)=
\begin{cases}
2j,&1\le j\le6,\\
14+v_2(5-3x/128),&j=7,\\
j+7,&j\ge8.
\end{cases} \tag{4}
\]
At \(j=7\), \(x/128\) is a 2-unit and \(v_2(5-3x/128)\ge1\). Thus the **exact** necessary 2-/3-adic alignment is \(q=6j\) for \(j\le6\), \(q=3(j+7)\) for \(j\ge8\), or \(q=3(14+\kappa)\), \(\kappa\ge1\), for \(j=7\). The middle formula is intentionally not extended into the exceptional seventh-order cancellation case.

## Theorem 2 — the two previously untreated numerator-divisible primes

For any reduced \(0<m<d\), suppose \(7\mid m\) and put \(j=v_7(m)\).
Writing \(r=v_7(1-\beta x)\) in the \(j=2\) case, the exact 7-adic pairs are
\[
(v_7(R),v_7(S))=
\begin{cases}
(-1,w),\quad w\ge1,&j=1,\\
(r,r+1),\quad r\ge0,&j=2,\\
(0,3-j),&j\ge3.
\end{cases} \tag{5}
\]
For \(j=2\), \(r\ge1\) **iff** \((m/49)d^{-1}\equiv2\pmod7\).
Thus the 7-adic test proves irrationality for \(j=1\), \(j\ge4\), and \(j=2\) outside that single residue; it is inconclusive for \(j=3\) and the exceptional \(j=2\) lift.

For \(13\mid m\), put \(j=v_{13}(m)\). The exact 13-adic pairs are
\[
(v_{13}(R),v_{13}(S))=
\begin{cases}
(r,r),\quad r=v_{13}(1-\beta x)\ge0,&j=1,\\
(0,1-j),&j\ge2.
\end{cases} \tag{6}
\]
For \(j=1\), \(r\ge1\) **iff** \((m/13)d^{-1}\equiv12\pmod{13}\), equivalently \(x\equiv156\pmod{169}\). Thus every \(j\ge2\), plus precisely this certified \(j=1\) subfamily, has irrational phase by the 13-adic test. Remaining cases are not declared rational.

**Proof.** For \(v_7(x)=j\ge1\), \(1-x\) and \(1+\gamma x\) are 7-units, \(v_7(u)=0\), \(v_7(1-u)=1\), and \(v_7(a)=j-2\). At \(j=1\), \(v_7(1-\beta x)=-1\), and \(v_7(b)\ge1\). At \(j\ge2\), \(v_7(b)=1\); \(v_7(1-\beta x)=0\) for \(j\ge3\), while for \(j=2\) it is \(r=v_7(1-3(x/49)/13)\). The unique mod-7 zero for \(x/49\) is \(13/3\equiv2\). Substitute in \(v_7(S)=v_7(b)+v_7(R)-v_7(a)\) to obtain (5).

For \(v_{13}(x)=j\ge1\), \(1-x\), \(1+\gamma x\), \(u\), and \(b\) are 13-units (notably \(u\not\equiv1\pmod{13}\)); \(v_{13}(a)=j-1\). At \(j\ge2\), \(1-\beta x\) is a unit; at \(j=1\), it is \(1-3(x/13)/49\), whose unique mod-13 zero is \(49/3\equiv12\). This proves (6). Each certified pair violates (1), since it has zero against nonzero, opposite signs, equal *nonzero* valuations, or \(|v_p(R)|\ge |v_p(S)|>0\) with a common sign. QED.

## Corollary — four-prime compatibility in the EC49FVD survivor

Suppose \(\gcd(md,91)=1\), and \(x\) lies in the old paired exceptional lift
\[
x\equiv1814\pmod{2401},\qquad x\equiv157\pmod{169}.
\]
Write \(r=v_7(a)\ge2\), \(s=v_{13}(a)\ge1\). If additionally \(6\mid m\), every *hypothetical rational phase* requires
\[
\boxed{r=2s,\qquad v_2(a)=2s,\qquad v_3(m)=6s.} \tag{7}
\]
Indeed the old 7-/13-adic pairs require \(h/k=2/(2+r)=1/(1+s)\), while (2) requires \(h/k=2/(2+A)=6/(6+q)\). This extends the old \((r,s,q)\) relation with an independent 2-adic coordinate.

### Strict new four-prime witness

Take the reduced rational width
\[
\boxed{x=\frac{481394062332}{646039432585}}.
\]
It is constructed by CRT with numerator residues
\[
m\equiv(4,\ 729,\ 1814,\ 157)
\pmod{(8,\ 3^7,\ 7^5,\ 13^3)},
\]
and denominator \(d=1+8\cdot3^7\cdot7^5\cdot13^3\), so that \(d\equiv1\) modulo every listed prime power. Exact valuations give
\[
v_7(a)=2,\quad v_{13}(a)=1,\quad v_3(m)=6,\quad v_2(a)=4,
\]
and
\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrr}
p&2&3&7&13\\\hline
v_p(R)&-2&-6&-2&-1\\
v_p(S)&-6&-12&-4&-2
\end{array}
\]
Thus **7, 13 and 3 all permit** the same rational candidate \(t=1/2\), while **2 forces** \(t=1/3\), a contradiction. This witness is therefore *not excluded by the three displayed 7-/13-/3-adic constraints alone* but is strictly excluded by the new four-prime synchronization. It does not claim that every other prime or predecessor certificate is inconclusive.

## Exact computational evidence and limits

Run \`python EC49FVE_MIXED_NUMERATOR_ADIC_VERIFY.py\` (Python 3, standard library only). Its actual local output:

\`\`\`
FINITE_FRACTION_CROSSCHECK_PASS {'two_three_both': 4021, 'two_three_mismatch': 4021, 'seven_numerator': 6075, 'seven_certified': 5893, 'thirteen_numerator': 3480, 'thirteen_certified': 518}
FOUR_PRIME_JOINT_EXCEPTION_WITNESS_PASS 481394062332/646039432585 {2: (-2, -6), 3: (-6, -12), 7: (-2, -4), 13: (-1, -2)}
ALL PASS
\`\`\`

The program exhausts **every reduced** \(0<m<d\le400\), checking (2), (5), (6) and their valid implications; the universal theorems follow from the **analytic valuation proofs**, not finite enumeration. No float approximations are used in the checker; the executable also recomputes the CRT witness. The 4021/4021 observed mixed-numerator mismatches are a declared *finite-range statistic*, not an assertion of all-width inequality.

**Next:** classify the joint exceptional infinite families satisfying (7), especially \(v_2(m)=7\) where the exact 2-adic cancellation order varies; alternatively find a new prime test that excludes all alignments or an actual rational-phase counterexample. Preserve original BRC source and independent owner/Activity gates.
